title: What the project label normal means
text: In this project, normal means the image classifier selected its normal category for the supplied image. It does not certify that both kidneys and the entire urinary tract are healthy. It does not establish kidney function or exclude infection, microscopic disease, an unseen lesion or a finding outside the model's training classes. Use the radiologist's report and clinical assessment.

title: Understanding estimated GFR

title: Why a urine albumin test matters
text: Albumin is a blood protein. Excess albumin in urine can signal kidney damage. A urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, often called uACR, helps assess this. A normal-looking scan does not replace urine testing when it is indicated, and a single result should be interpreted by a clinician.

title: Use risk-based kidney checks
text: NIDDK recommends kidney checks for people with diabetes, high blood pressure, heart disease or a family history of kidney failure. It advises yearly checks for diabetes; for other risks, discuss the interval with a clinician. Do not impose annual scans or one testing schedule on everyone.

title: Diabetes care protects kidney health

The normal image category does not show whether blood glucose is controlled or whether early diabetes-related kidney damage is present. Discuss laboratory results rather than relying on the image label.
